title: Notation
body_md: Bold lowercase and uppercase letters denote vectors and matrices, respectively. The operators $(\cdot)^*$, $(\cdot)^{\mathtt{T}}$, $(\cdot)^{\mathtt{H}}$, and $\operatorname{Tr}(\cdot)$ denote conjugation, transpose, Hermitian transpose, and trace, respectively. The symbols $|\cdot|$, $\|\cdot\|$, and $\mathbb{E}[\cdot]$ denote absolute value, Euclidean norm, and expectation, respectively. We write $\dot y_x=\partial y/\partial x$, and use $\Re(\cdot)$ and $\Im(\cdot)$ for real and imaginary parts. The notation $\mathcal{CN}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\boldsymbol{R})$ denotes a circularly symmetric complex Gaussian distribution with mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance $\boldsymbol{R}$.

title: {\bf{Remark}}
body_md: Conventional FD-ISAC architectures suffer from severe uplink-to-downlink interference~\cite{Tang_2026, Liu_2023}. Exploiting asymmetric MEC traffic, we defer downlink to Phase 3. Reserving Phase 2 for uplink transmission and sensing avoids simultaneous uplink and downlink data transmission.

title: Proof
body_md: To derive the closed-form CRLBs, we invert the decoupled $2 \times 2$ angular FIM $\boldsymbol{J}_{\theta,\phi}$ in \eqref{eq:equip_FIM}. For a $2 \times 2$ matrix block, the diagonal entries of its inverse $\boldsymbol{J}_{\theta,\phi}^{-1}$ explicitly yield the effective parameter bounds. We use $J_{xy} = \Psi(\boldsymbol{p}, \rho) \rho \tilde{c}_{xy}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}})$ to isolate  $\mathcal{G}_\theta(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}})$ and $\mathcal{G}_\phi(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}})$. Factoring out $[\Psi(\boldsymbol{p}, \rho)\rho]^{-1}$ yields \eqref{eq:CRLB_theta} and \eqref{eq:CRLB_phi}.
